name: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
problem: MoE scales parameters at constant FLOPs, but adoption was blocked by routing complexity, expert communication cost, and training instability.
mechanism: Sparse encoder-decoder (T5) where each Transformer FFN block is replaced by N experts and a single scalar gating network sends each token to the top-1 expert only. Gating computes a router projection followed by softmax over N experts, and the layer dispatches the token to argmax only; dropping the second expert halves the expert-weight bytes read per token versus top-2 MoE. Load balance is an auxiliary loss f = N * sum_i f_i * P_i (importance probability P, routed-token fraction f) added to the LM loss at alpha=1e-2, plus a z-loss on the logits. Enables bfloat16 mixed precision at scale via stochastic rounding of the residual add. Active-vs-total: Switch-Base 15B total / 11B active (about 73 percent); Switch-Extra Huge 1.6T total / roughly 140B active. Serving consequence: only the active experts are computed, but all expert weights must stay resident in HBM, so the 1.6T model cannot be served on a single device regardless of the low active count; weights are expert-sharded and activations move all-to-all each layer.
speedup_reported: Up to 7x faster pre-training than T5-Base at matched compute and step count, and 4x faster than T5-XXL at matched compute; switching from top-2 to top-1 gating also roughly doubled training throughput at matched quality in the authors' own ablation. Original experiments ran on TPU pods (32 TPU v3/v4 devices in the reported configurations). These are compute-matched rather than wall-clock-matched comparisons, so 7x is not 7x less wall time.
notes:
Venue is JMLR 2022, confirmed via Semantic Scholar ('Journal of machine learning research'), but the paper schema's venue enum has no JMLR entry so this is recorded as 'other'; the authoritative venue is in notes.  Load balancing here is auxiliary-loss based, NOT auxiliary-loss-free; DeepSeek-V3's bias-term contribution is explicitly contrasted against this. Token-choice top-1 gating of this form is the shape vLLM's sparse MoE block expects: an experts module receiving hidden_states, top_k_index and top_k_weights.
